rationale:
Final design: I keep the revised design unchanged, so it races as written (kd 0.6, all else as the raced iteration-2 design).

What the evidence shows: the kd change from 0.2 to 0.4 (iteration 2 to 4) is the only factor that moved the outcome. It raised oval finishes from 0 to 6 of 20 and the score from 52.11 to 220.09. The s-bend and slalom still ended off track in all 40 trials, at progress 0.26 and 0.17, with max_error about 0.064 to 0.067 m. Steering oscillation and control effort both rose, but the robot still finished.

What I accepted from the round-2 critique: (a) the s-bend and slalom gain from kd 0.4 was modest, so I do not claim kd fixes those tracks. (b) I must state a noise limit. An assumed signal-rate noise of about 2 units/s gives about 1.2 turn (about 420 PWM) at kd 0.6, which stays below the base PWM of about 3276 at speed 1.6. This is an assumed figure, not a measurement. (c) The oscillation rise is a real cost to track.

What I rejected: (a) changing base_speed. The critique is right that base 1.6 is not what produced the finishes, so my earlier attribution was wrong. But this race is a single-factor test of kd, and changing speed would confound it. (b) Moving to line-loss recovery (search modes or stop) in this race. The critique's point that the excursion starts at the first line loss is plausible and important, but it is a different factor and would break the one-factor test. I will test it next if kd 0.6 is neutral on s-bend and slalom. (c) Changing kp or the sensor span now. The critique's argument that the 0.065 m excursion is driven by kp is untested, and I have no race evidence that kp moves it.

Decision rule: keep kd 0.6 if oval mean score or finish rate rises above the kd 0.4 run (483.5 oval mean, 30 percent finish), or if s-bend or slalom progress exceeds 0.26 and 0.17. If progress on s-bend and slalom falls, or steering oscillation is high enough to drop the oval finish rate, kd 0.4 is the ceiling and the next race tests line-loss recovery.

Expected results (hypotheses, not data): oval finishes stay near or above 30 percent, progress on s-bend and slalom is similar or slightly higher, and max_error stays near 0.06 m. Completion on s-bend and slalom remains unlikely at this speed.
